revenue: Consolidated net sales rose 18% to $382.1 billion for the six months (20% in Q2), led by AWS at +33% on higher customer usage (partly offset by price concessions on long-term contracts) and by North America (+14%) and International (+17%) on higher unit volumes, third-party seller activity, advertising and subscriptions. FX was a tailwind of roughly $3.0 billion YTD, though it was immaterial in Q2 itself.
gross_profit: Amazon does not present gross profit (management states operating income is the more meaningful measure), but cost of sales fell to 48.0% of net sales YTD from 48.8%, i.e. implied gross margin widened ~80bps. The dollar increase in cost of sales reflects higher product and shipping costs on greater volume, offset by operational efficiencies, IEEPA tariff refunds received in Q2 2026, and the growing mix of higher-margin AWS, advertising and third-party seller revenue (AWS costs sit in technology and infrastructure, not cost of sales).
operating_income: Operating income grew to $51.3 billion YTD from $37.6 billion, lifting operating margin to roughly 13.4% from 11.6%. AWS drove the bulk of it ($30.8 billion vs $21.7 billion) on sales growth net of heavy infrastructure spend, while North America and International benefited from unit and advertising growth; operating leverage on fulfillment (14.9% of sales vs 15.6%), sales and marketing (5.8% vs 6.5%) and G&A (1.4% vs 1.7%) more than offset technology and infrastructure rising to 16.4% of sales from 15.5% on depreciation and AI/infrastructure investment.
interest_expense: Interest expense roughly doubled to $2.1 billion YTD (from $1.1 billion) and to $1.3 billion in Q2, driven by new Notes issuances and finance leases — consistent with $82.4 billion of debt proceeds raised in the first half to fund record capital spending and strategic investments.
pre_tax: Pre-tax income was inflated far beyond operating performance by $69.1 billion of other income, net (vs $3.9 billion), almost entirely non-cash upward fair value adjustments on the Anthropic nonvoting preferred stock and reclassification gains on converted Anthropic convertible notes; higher interest expense was an immaterial offset. The associated $15.9 billion of discrete tax expense on those Anthropic marks drove the tax provision to $27.8 billion.
current_assets: The filing does not present a balance sheet discussion of current assets or liabilities. It does note cash, cash equivalents and marketable securities were flat at $123.0 billion between December 31, 2025 and June 30, 2026 despite $96.3 billion of capex and $39.8 billion of acquisition/investment outflows, with the gap funded by $71.4 billion of operating cash flow and $82.4 billion of new debt proceeds; management states liquidity is sufficient for at least the next twelve months.
inventory: Inventory balances and turnover are not separately discussed. The only data point is the sensitivity disclosure that a 1% incremental valuation allowance would add roughly $405 million to cost of sales, implying inventory of about $40.5 billion at June 30, 2026; the filing offers no explanation of any period-over-period change.
total_debt: Total debt rose materially: first-half proceeds from short-term and long-term debt were $82.4 billion versus $4.7 billion a year ago, against only $19.5 billion of combined debt, finance lease and financing obligation repayments, plus $2.1 billion of equipment acquired under finance leases. The borrowing funded the step-up in capex and the OpenAI/Anthropic equity investments; no revolver or commercial paper was outstanding at quarter end, and management expects additional financing activity in 2026.
ebitda: LTM EBITDA is not disclosed but clearly expanded — operating income grew $13.7 billion year over year in the first half on AWS strength and retail cost leverage, and depreciation and amortization is rising sharply with the technology and infrastructure build-out, which adds back into EBITDA. LTM operating cash flow of $161.4 billion (up from $121.1 billion) corroborates the cash earnings improvement.
leverage: Gross leverage pressure is building because debt is growing much faster than earnings — roughly $82 billion of new borrowings in six months versus a $13.7 billion increase in first-half operating income — but the starting point is very low and EBITDA growth plus $123 billion of cash and marketable securities keeps net leverage modest. The key watch item is that free cash flow swung to negative $7.6 billion LTM (from +$18.2 billion) as capex reached $169 billion, meaning incremental investment is now debt-funded.
operating_cash: Operating cash flow rose to $71.4 billion for the six months from $49.5 billion, and to $161.4 billion on an LTM basis from $121.1 billion, which management attributes to higher net income excluding non-cash items plus favorable working capital swings; lower cash taxes paid ($4.0 billion YTD vs $5.6 billion, aided by the retroactive 2026 Notice) also helped. Cash conversion against debt service remains very strong even as free cash flow turned negative on capex.
debt_service: Debt service costs are climbing — interest expense doubled to $2.1 billion YTD and scheduled repayments of debt, finance leases and financing obligations rose to $19.5 billion from $7.2 billion — but coverage remains comfortable against $161.4 billion of LTM operating cash flow and $1.3 billion of quarterly interest income. Management flags that rising rates and higher borrowing levels could increase future borrowing costs.
guidance: No full-year revenue or EBITDA guidance is provided; the company guides only one quarter ahead. Q3 2026 guidance (issued July 30, 2026) is net sales of $197.0–$202.0 billion (+9% to +12%, including an ~80bps FX headwind) and operating income of $22.5–$26.5 billion versus $17.4 billion in Q3 2025. Adding first-half actuals of $382.1 billion of net sales and $51.3 billion of operating income implies nine-month totals of roughly $579.1 billion / $73.8 billion at the low end, $581.6 billion / $75.8 billion at the midpoint, and $584.1 billion / $77.8 billion at the high end.
